what: A dead letter queue (DLQ) is a side queue where messages go after failing too many times. The main queue keeps flowing while you study and replay the failures.
like: Like the post office's undeliverable mail desk: letters that keep bouncing are set aside for a person to check, so the rest of the mail still goes out.
why: One bad message (a poison message) cannot block or slow every other job
Failed work is kept safe for debugging instead of being lost
After a fix you can replay the failures with one redrive

nodes.t: Engineer + logs|find and fix the bug

steps.d: The AI engine puts a job on the source queue, for example 'summarise page 42'. A worker receives it and starts processing.
If the worker crashes or errors, it never deletes the message. After the visibility timeout (a hidden pause) the message shows up again and the receive count goes up by one.
The redrive policy sets maxReceiveCount. Once a message is received that many times without being deleted, the queue moves it to the DLQ.
An alarm watches how many messages sit in the DLQ. Anything above zero means real failures that need a person or an automatic triage job.
In SQS standard queues the clock keeps the original enqueue time, so set DLQ retention longer than the source queue or failures quietly expire.
After the bug is fixed, redrive moves messages back to the source queue. Workers check an idempotency key so jobs that already half-succeeded are not done twice.

choices.d: How many tries before a message is parked. Too low (1) sends messages to the DLQ on one hiccup; too high lets a poison message burn worker time for hours.
Visibility timeout sets the pause before a retry. Make it longer than the slowest normal job, and use backoff (longer waits each try) for rate limited LLM APIs.
Set it longer than the source queue's retention, ideally the 14 day maximum, so you have time to investigate before messages expire.
Alarm on DLQ depth above zero for critical jobs. For noisy jobs alert on the rate of new arrivals instead, so the team is not paged for one stray message.
Manual redrive after a fix, or an automatic job that retries later. Always pair it with idempotent handlers and a cap so a still broken message cannot loop forever.

instead.why: Stop calling a failing dependency at all instead of parking each message
Keep the log and use a retry topic plus a DLQ topic
The main queue itself; the DLQ is one feature beside it

breaks.d: No redrive policy, so a bad message is retried again and again.
breaks.see: Same message ID in error logs every few minutes; worker CPU busy with no progress
breaks.fix: Add a redrive policy with a sensible maxReceiveCount and a DLQ

breaks.d: Messages land in the DLQ but no one is watching.
breaks.see: Users report missing results days later; DLQ visible count growing
breaks.fix: CloudWatch alarm on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible for the DLQ, routed to on-call

breaks.d: DLQ retention equals or is shorter than the source queue, and the original enqueue time is kept.
breaks.see: DLQ empties itself though nobody redrove it
breaks.fix: Give the DLQ a longer retention than the source

breaks.d: Some jobs half-succeeded before failing, then run again.
breaks.see: Double charges, duplicate emails or two copies of the same row
breaks.fix: Idempotency keys and upserts so reprocessing the same message is safe

breaks.d: Visibility timeout is shorter than normal processing time, so slow jobs look failed.
breaks.see: DLQ messages that succeed when replayed unchanged
breaks.fix: Raise the visibility timeout or extend it while the job runs

say: Every async queue gets a dead letter queue: after about five failed receives the message is parked there, so one poison message never blocks the rest.
I alarm on DLQ depth, keep DLQ retention longer than the source queue, and log the error with the message ID so it is easy to trace.
Handlers are idempotent with a job key, so once we ship a fix we can redrive the whole DLQ back to the source safely.
For our AI jobs, a timeout from the model provider is retried with backoff, but a page the parser cannot read goes straight to the DLQ.

followups.a: Count how many retries a temporary problem needs to clear, like a short LLM rate limit, then add a little room. Three to five is common. Pair it with backoff so the retries are spread out rather than instant.

Not built into the broker. Consumers commit offsets, so you write failures to your own retry or DLQ topic. Kafka Connect offers one for sink connectors through errors.tolerance=all and errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name.

Transient errors, like timeouts or 429 rate limits, deserve retries with backoff. Permanent ones, like bad input or a schema mismatch, will never pass, so send them to the DLQ early and save worker time.
A DLQ can break strict ordering, because a parked message is skipped while later ones go ahead. If order really matters, AWS advises not using a DLQ there and handling failures in the app.

check.q: You redrive 1,000 failed jobs. What keeps reprocessing safe?
check.a: Idempotent handlers using a job key
check.why: Some jobs may have partly run, so running them again must not double the effect.

check.why: It shows how many failures are waiting in the DLQ right now.
